release.content: pubkit 0.12.2 was released on 2026-10-22 from commit 00b26ae71a45047103b00e6e994da27f52dcc93b with these changes.

rows: Per-language update and security settings in pubkit.json: "update": {"rust", "node", "python"} turns each language's dependency updates in the nightly pull request on or off ("update": false turns them all off, leaving the pub* pins), and "security": {"fuzz": {"rust": false}} keeps a scheduled rust-ci run's fuzzing as brief as any other. With updates on, the nightly pull request also moves the npm packages within their package.json ranges and re-locks tests/requirements.lock. An unknown setting stops the nightly

node-ci and python-ci run an audit job on every run, part of passed: npm audit of package-lock.json, and pip-audit of the hash-locked requirements (audit-requirements, by default tests/requirements.lock). A known advisory fails CI; there is no switch
pubkit pins moves pubkit's pin in python-ci, node-ci and service-ci workflows too, not only rust-ci
OSV-Scanner (every lockfile, on every run) and GitHub dependency review (public pull requests) in rust-ci, node-ci and python-ci, both part of passed, with no switch

security.dependabot in pubkit.json: pubkit sync and init write .github/dependabot.yml from its schedule, ecosystems and options (default: weekly GitHub Actions updates; false leaves the file to the repository), and security.sonar.args adds SonarQube Cloud properties to every sonar job

Property tests: tests/requirements-pubkit.txt pins Hypothesis for every package, and pubkit's pytest plugin gives each Hypothesis property PUBKIT_FUZZ_RUNS inputs, with no deadline. python-ci and node-ci set it: fuzz-runs (100) on every push and pull request, fuzz-runs-scheduled (10000) on a scheduled run. security.fuzz now defaults to on for python and node, as for rust, and false keeps a scheduled run as brief as any other. A Node package's fast-check reads it through fc.configureGlobal

pubkit protect also puts a ruleset on each repository's release tags (src/pubkit/tag-ruleset.json): nobody may create, move or delete a v* tag, and only GitHub Actions, where pubrel tag runs after a release pull request merges, may bypass it. protect --check reports a repository without it
